\subsection{T5 -- Fault injection and recovery}
Executed on 2026-10-21 (09:34--10:17 CEST). Two concurrent open-loop
streams were submitted through the FarmersMSP gateway peer: \texttt{RegisterProduction} at 32\,TPS and
\texttt{VerifyByUID} at 64\,TPS (20\% of the maximum sustainable rates measured in T2). Each run consisted of
60\,s of normal operation, a 30\,s fault window and 90\,s of observation after
restoration; each fault was repeated 3 times. In the test-network each peer is attached to two
Docker networks; the first F4 series disconnected peer0.producers from only one of them (reported as F4p), and F4 was therefore
repeated disconnecting the peer from all its networks (10:34--10:46 CEST). After each run, every submitted write was reconciled against the
ledger of both peers (\texttt{qscc GetTransactionByID}), every committed lot was read back from both peers, and the block
heights of the two peers were compared.

\paragraph{Observations.}
\begin{itemize}
  \item \textbf{F1 (peer (producers) stopped).} Expected: writes unavailable (endorsement policy requires both organisations); reads through the Farmers peer unaffected. Observed: longest write gap
        31.0\,s, writes recovered 1.0\,s after restoration (dominant write failures: \texttt{ENDORSE:GRPC\_UNAVAILABLE (2513), ENDORSE:GRPC\_ABORTED (461)});
        longest read gap 1.6\,s (read failures: \texttt{none}). Of the writes submitted during the fault
        window, 0.0\% eventually succeeded (per run: 0, 0, 0\%), with a
        maximum latency of --\,s.
  \item \textbf{F2 (orderer stopped).} Expected: writes cannot be ordered; reads unaffected. Observed: longest write gap
        44.6\,s, writes recovered 14.5\,s after restoration (dominant write failures: \texttt{SUBMIT:GRPC\_UNAVAILABLE (4276)});
        longest read gap 1.0\,s (read failures: \texttt{none}). Of the writes submitted during the fault
        window, 0.0\% eventually succeeded (per run: 0, 0, 0\%), with a
        maximum latency of --\,s.
  \item \textbf{F3 (chaincode container killed).} Expected: requests needing the killed chaincode container fail or are delayed until the peer relaunches it. Observed: longest write gap
        0.5\,s, writes recovered 0.0\,s after restoration (dominant write failures: \texttt{none});
        longest read gap 0.5\,s (read failures: \texttt{none}). Of the writes submitted during the fault
        window, 100.0\% eventually succeeded (per run: 100, 100, 100\%), with a
        maximum latency of 2.8\,s, i.e.\ they were delayed until the component became available again rather than rejected.
  \item \textbf{F4p (peer (producers): one of two networks removed).} Expected: writes interrupted until the peers re-establish their connection through the remaining network. Observed: longest write gap
        14.8\,s, writes recovered 0.5\,s after restoration (dominant write failures: \texttt{ENDORSE:GRPC\_ABORTED (1388)});
        longest read gap 0.9\,s (read failures: \texttt{none}). Of the writes submitted during the fault
        window, 51.9\% eventually succeeded (per run: 28, 100, 28\%), with a
        maximum latency of 1.0\,s, i.e.\ they were delayed until the component became available again rather than rejected.
  \item \textbf{F4 (peer (producers) fully partitioned).} Expected: as F1, without stopping the peer process. Observed: longest write gap
        33.0\,s, writes recovered 3.0\,s after restoration (dominant write failures: \texttt{ENDORSE:GRPC\_ABORTED (2275), ENDORSE:GRPC\_UNAVAILABLE (893)});
        longest read gap 1.5\,s (read failures: \texttt{none}). Of the writes submitted during the fault
        window, 0.0\% eventually succeeded (per run: 0, 0, 0\%), with a
        maximum latency of --\,s.
  \item \textbf{State after recovery.} In 15 of 15 runs the ledger was consistent after recovery:
        74594 of 74594 client-confirmed writes were committed as valid on both peers,
        0 writes with an unknown client outcome were found committed and 4276 were not committed,
        0 discrepancies were found, and 0 of 149188 lot read-backs failed. No transaction was lost after confirmation, and no rejected transaction was committed.
  \item \textbf{Scope.} With one peer per organisation, an endorsement policy requiring both organisations and a single-node
        ordering service, F1, F2 and F4 necessarily interrupt state-changing operations; the experiment characterises the
        availability and the recovery of the tested topology, not the fault tolerance of Fabric deployments with redundant
        peers or a multi-node Raft cluster.
\end{itemize}
